title: 3D Gaussian Splatting Data Compression via Adaptive Residual Quantization and Error Compensation
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-fidelity novel-view synthesis with real-time rendering, but high-quality scenes require many Gaussian primitives, incurring substantial storage overhead. Anchor-based representations reduce storage, yet high-dimensional anchor features remain a storage bottleneck, and their quantization errors can propagate through attribute prediction. Fixed-depth quantization cannot adapt to different rate--distortion requirements across anchors, while nearest-neighbor index assignment ignores coding costs. To address these limitations, we present a 3DGS compression framework based on \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}esidual \textbf{Q}uantization and \textbf{E}rror \textbf{C}ompensation (ARQEC). We encode anchor features with three-stage residual vector quantization (RVQ) and adaptively select the quantization depth for each anchor. A Context Refiner uses spatial hash-grid context to compensate for feature residuals remaining after RVQ. An Attribute Adapter further refines the quantized offsets and scaling based on the recovered features, reducing the impact of quantization errors on Gaussian attribute prediction. Finally, a contextual entropy model estimates conditional code lengths for quantization depth and RVQ index symbols. A local rate--distortion criterion generates candidate assignments, followed by rendering-based calibration on held-out views. Extensive experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending show that our method achieves $47\times$--$157\times$ full-model compression over vanilla 3DGS while maintaining high rendering quality. Compared with Hash-grid Assisted Context (HAC), it achieves up to $1.53\times$ additional compression in full-model size, yielding a competitive trade-off between model compactness and rendering fidelity.

cited_by.name: Adaptive Residual Vector Quantization (ARQ) with Context-Guided Recovery
